title: Our galaxy revealed with the VLTI
caption: The Milky Way beside an Auxiliary Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way stretches across the sky next to one of the four 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in a photograph taken during the ESO Ultra HD Expedition.

These smaller telescopes do not work only on their own. Together with the four Unit Telescopes, whose main mirrors are 8.2 m across, they can be linked to form a giant 'interferometer' called the ESO Very Large Telescope Interferometer. By combining the light collected by several telescopes spread out on the mountain, an interferometer can see far finer detail than any one of them could manage alone.

ESO describes the combination as the world's most advanced optical instrument for exploring the depths of the Universe. On this night the Auxiliary Telescope stands beneath the band of the Milky Way, part of the galaxy it helps astronomers to study.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure can gather far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way may look brighter and more detailed than it would to someone standing there.
